tagline: Home to Europe's largest superyacht marina and the global hub for yacht crew — the densest concentration of marine wealth and expertise on the Mediterranean coast.
summary: Antibes is the beating heart of Mediterranean yachting. Port Vauban is widely regarded as Europe's largest marina, with around 1,500–1,700 berths including a superyacht quay (the IYCA) able to host vessels up to 165 metres. The town is also the global capital for superyacht crew, with an estimated 30,000 crew passing through each year alongside the captains, brokers and refit yards that cluster around the harbour. Add the luxury hotels of Cap d'Antibes and the day-trip flows of Juan-les-Pins, and Antibes concentrates more marine wealth, vessels and on-water expertise than anywhere else on the coast — a natural anchor for a premium foiling network linking the marina to Cannes, Nice, Monaco and the islands.

use_cases.title: Marina & superyacht guest transfers
use_cases.body: Foiling tenders and shuttles move owners and guests between Port Vauban, anchored superyachts and the Cap d'Antibes hotels, then on to Cannes, Monaco or the Nice airport. A smooth, near-silent transfer that matches the marina's flagship clientele.

use_cases.title: Crew & marine-industry shuttle
use_cases.body: A frequent foiling service connecting the superyacht crew hub at Antibes with the wider Riviera's harbours and refit yards. It moves the coast's marine workforce quickly and cleanly, bypassing the gridlocked A8 and coast road.

use_cases.title: Riviera coastal & island excursions
use_cases.body: On-demand foiling runs from Antibes to Cannes, the car-free Lérins Islands and Nice, with the hybrid platform reaching open-water destinations like Saint-Tropez and Corsica. Visitors swap the queue for a signature on-water experience.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Antibes' core legs all sit inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope on calm coastal water — Antibes→Cannes (~6 nm), Antibes→Nice airport (~9 nm) and Antibes→Monaco (~16 nm) — with margin for frequent rotations serving both the superyacht guests and the marine workforce concentrated at Port Vauban.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The 2,000 nm hybrid range unlocks longer corridors beyond the electric envelope or where charging isn't viable — down-coast to Saint-Tropez (~40 nm) and across open water to Corsica (~100 nm) or the Italian Riviera — as premium experiential cruises for the marina's high-end clientele.
